Prose:
The guard’s hand retreated, the staff lowering completely to resume its idle posture against his shoulder. Caelen allowed himself one sharp exhale, the sound swallowed instantly by the heavy air of the pen. It was not freedom; it was merely a pause in the countdown to the next beat, a respite purchased with a calculated lie. He stepped back further, creating a deliberate buffer zone between himself, the guard’s weapon, and the young woman who still shook violently on the stone floor.

He used the lull in violence to map the enclosure with his eyes. The pale yellow light filtering through high slits revealed thirty other captives huddled against the far walls, their forms indistinct blobs of rags and soot in the gloom. The gravity here was a physical weight; every shift of his own center of mass required a conscious effort to counteract the pull, making him feel anchored down as if the very ground were trying to crush him. Outside the gate, he noted the patrol rhythm: two figures with spears resting casually against their shoulders, moving without urgency but watching everything.

Inside the pen, the hierarchy was stark and shifting. The scarred man, once an apparent authority figure slumped near an overturned crate, now looked like discarded furniture, his dignity shattered by the masked man in purple. The overseer sat at a rickety table, flipping pages of a ledger with rhythmic indifference while tapping a black-tipped cane against the stone floor. He had not looked up from his writing, but Caelen knew that gaze was all-encompassing; it weighed the entire room.

Caelen forced a calmness that felt alien on his tongue. He accepted his constrained agency as the only currency available right now. Pain and confusion were not obstacles; they were the conditions of his existence here. He would be the idiot they wanted him to be, and in that role, perhaps he might find a way to survive long enough to stop being one. He shifted his weight cautiously, testing the limits of his restraints without drawing attention, ready to play the fool again if needed.
